title: AgenticMail bridge-wake -- T1566 unverified-sender inbound email resumes a privileged agent session
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-57495 (GHSA-fq4x-789w-jg5h,
CVSS 8.2 HIGH), a self-reported advisory for AgenticMail, which gives AI
agents real email addresses.

Prior to the patched versions, `handleBridgeMail` (`dispatcher.ts:2045`)
acted on any inbound email routed to the bridge inbox WITHOUT verifying
the sender is the operator, then called `planBridgeWake()` and
`composeBridgeWakePrompt` (`host-bridge.ts:141`), which embeds the
attacker-controlled `from`/`subject`/`preview` fields VERBATIM into the
prompt a resumed agent session reads. `resumeBridgeSession`
(`bridge-wake.ts:103`) then runs that prompt with
`permissionMode: 'bypassPermissions'` -- an indirect prompt injection
into a fully-privileged agent (Bash/Write/Edit/WebFetch plus the
agenticmail MCP toolbelt) running as the operator's own OAuth identity.
The advisory notes a sibling handler in the same codebase
(`inbound.ts:102`, the operator-query email-reply hook) DOES gate on
`isOperatorReplySender(replyFrom, config.operatorEmail)` -- the
higher-privilege bridge-wake path had no equivalent check, which is the
precise asymmetry the fix closes.

Detection logic flags an AgenticMail bridge-wake event whose own log
output shows `resumeBridgeSession`/`bypassPermissions` firing without a
corresponding `isOperatorReplySender` gate having run first -- on an
unpatched install this condition is systemic (every inbound email to the
bridge triggers it, not only attacker-sent ones), which is stated plainly
in falsepositives below rather than implied as attack-specific.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (agenticmail, via
GHSA and NVD), fixed in @agenticmail/claudecode 0.2.39,
@agenticmail/codex 0.1.33, @agenticmail/core 0.9.43,
@agenticmail/openclaw 0.5.71.
